replacements.name: native priority
replacements.new:
calling a foreign exception's __context__ property. No Python-level linking/overwriting.
    V6 selection: a non-Exception primary (KeyboardInterrupt/SystemExit/...) outranks an ORDINARY completion
    secondary and propagates by bare re-raise after the secondary handler ends, so its own context is not rewritten
    and no caller can absorb it as an ordinary failure; otherwise the secondary propagates. Both objects stay in
    the transaction's retained exceptions (CensusLog.exceptions) either way."""
    _check(state, stage, pid, 'before')
    try:
        value = function(*args, **kwargs)
    except BaseException as primary:
        try:
            _check(state, stage, pid, 'after failed')
        except BaseException as secondary:
            state.keep(primary)
            state.keep(secondary)
            if _ordinary(primary) or not _ordinary(secondary):
                raise  # secondary selected; interpreter context keeps the primary
        state.keep(primary)  # identity-deduplicated: completion passed or the primary outranks an ordinary secondary
        raise
